correctness.rationale: The current-choice priority is lexicographic affordable-first then smaller MES price; within unavailable candidates score by nonnegative supporter budget. Candidate priority depends only on its own approver set and is monotone under adding approvers. Thus from an unsatisfied sincere winner, no unilateral current-round report can improve priority of a genuinely approved alternative or decrease the unapproved incumbent, proving immediate OSP even on the round where affordability disappears. After permanent halt, frozen-weight approval scoring is separable and monotone, and a winner is chosen each round. Standard MES prefix payments and the earliest-over-1/l budget contradiction establish wEJR for fully cohesive groups; appended winners cannot lower satisfaction. Stronger wEJR+ is claimed by inheritance from Phillips et al. Theorem 3.14 arbitrary-completion guarantee, but its exact full text could not independently be retrieved: this is a priority/premise verification risk, not an invented theorem proof. Independent exact fixed-state checks compared 13,344 one-round manipulation cases, with no violation.

originality.rationale: Full Borodin–Lueger 2026 paper (Section 4.3, page 9) proves OSP of uncompleted MES and explicitly poses preserving OSP after completion as an open question. Phillips et al. arbitrary-completion theorem supplies wEJR+ fairness, not OSP; weighted score monotonicity handles this new joint requirement. Classic weighted approval monotonicity is not itself original.

The source Borodin–Lueger paper explicitly asks if such completion can exist, making the answer directly motivated. Full-horizon strategyproofness is explicitly not asserted.

limitations: A fixed finite horizon and voter count are public; current-round OSP holds with past held fixed, not globally.
